about: Measured on the committed cases (test/benchmark/cases/regtest-v1) with the analysis as of the first run, 2026-10-26. Each number sits a little below (or, for a ceiling, a little above) what was measured, so an honest change passes and one that quietly makes a guess worse fails. A floor is not a target and not a claim about real data. If a change to the rules is right and moves a number past its floor, change the floor in the same commit and say why in the message. Keys are <case>:<path into the results of test/benchmark/lib/evaluate.js>.

payments:change.byTier.high.precision.p.why: a high guess has to stay right almost every time, or the label means nothing

peel-chains:change.byTier.high.precision.why: a high guess has to stay right almost every time, or the label means nothing

batch-consolidation:change.byTier.high.p.why: a high guess has to stay right almost every time, or the label means nothing

sweeps:change.byTier.high.precision.p.why: a high guess has to stay right almost every time, or the label means nothing

coinjoins:change.byTier.high.precision.p.why: a high guess has to stay right almost every time, or the label means nothing

payjoin:change.byTier.high.precision.p.why: a PayJoin is the transaction that breaks the change rules; one high guess was wrong in the first run

payments:change.byTier.medium.precision..why: medium must stay a better guess than a coin toss and than the always-answering baselines (the largest output is right 56%)

payments:change.precision.p.why: overall precision of the change guess on ordinary payments

payments:change.coverage.p.why: a change that stops guessing is safe but useless; the first run guessed on 79%

coinjoins:change.precision.p.why: the hardest case for the change guess: wallets that mix, and exchange payouts

coinjoins:coinjoin.recall.p.why: every real CoinJoin of the case was found in the first run

coinjoins:coinjoin.falsePositiveRate.p.why: a batched exchange payout with equal amounts looks like a CoinJoin (20% in the first run); it must not get worse

batch-consolidation:batch.recall.p.why: every batch payment was found in the first run

batch-consolidation:batch.precision.p.why: nothing but a batch was flagged as one

batch-consolidation:consolidation.recall.why: every consolidation was found in the first run

sweeps:batch.recall.p.why: every batch payment was found in the first run

sweeps:consolidation.recall.p.why: every sweep of deposit addresses was found in the first run

payjoin:consolidation.recall.p.why: every consolidation was found in the first run

payments:consolidation.falsePositiveRate.why: an ordinary payment that needs five coins is flagged as a consolidation (4.9% in the first run); it must not get worse

payments:clusters.precision.p.why: addresses spent together by one sender share an owner

peel-chains:clusters.precision.p.why: addresses spent together by one sender share an owner

batch-consolidation:clusters.precision.p.why: addresses spent together by one sender share an owner

sweeps:clusters.precision.p.why: addresses spent together by one sender share an owner

coinjoins:clusters.precision.p.why: a CoinJoin must not merge its owners into one cluster

coinjoins:clusters.recallOfWhatCoSpendin.why: the cost of the CoinJoin exclusion: exchange payouts wrongly flagged lose their clusters (65% found in the first run)

payjoin:clusters.precision.p.why: a PayJoin joins two owners and the rule cannot tell (95% in the first run); it must not get worse

peel-chains:peel.stepsFlagged.p.why: the steps of real chains that are in a detected chain (71% in the first run)

peel-chains:peel.real.p.why: a detected chain in the peel-chains case is a real one (93% in the first run)

payments:peel.notThereFlaggedPer1000Othe.why: ordinary payments out of one coin make the same shape as a peel chain (5.8 chains per 1,000 in the first run); it must not get worse

mainnet-sample:coinjoin.why: on real traffic a COINJOIN? flag is rare (2 of 4,671, both batches of dust-sized outputs); loosening the detector must show up here

mainnet-sample:consolidation.why: 3.5% of real transactions had 5 or more inputs into 1 or 2 outputs in the first run; the flag must not fire more often than that without a reason

mainnet-sample:batch.why: 3.2% of real transactions were flagged as a batch in the first run

mainnet-sample:peelInChain.why: 2.8% of real transactions are in a detected peel chain (3.6% before dust-sized peels were left out), counting only the neighbours that were in the sample; it must not fire more often

mainnet-sample:changeGuessed.why: a change guess was made on 71% of the real transactions that can have one; a change that stops guessing is safe but useless
